content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Sanctuary Rescue's PostSanctuary Rescue Verified accountSeptember 8, 2025 · Shared with PublicSeptember 8 - Let’s Learn About Lurchers!Why do we need to know about such an obscure dog breed, you ask? Well, because we have a lovely litter of lurcher littles looking for loving, lasting landings. So let’s learn about these sleek and graceful dogs!Apparently a lurcher is a cross between a sighthound (think Greyhounds or Whippets) and a working breed (think Collie or Kelpie). This can lead to a wide range of coat colors and sizes. Our lurchers seem very greyhound-ish and will likely be large in height and medium in weight with thin, sleek, wide-chested silhouettes like their racing ancestors. This family came from a breeder neglect seizure where there were 17+ of these unusual creatures living in a hellhole. This litter of lucky lurchers landed with us at just three weeks old and as a result have had excellent enrichment and socialization during their formative puppyhood. They are happy and silly and ready to leap into their forevers. Wanna know more about how cool these leggy, lean lurching machines are? Well, the interweb says, “They are intelligent, adaptable, and can be affectionate and playful companions.” Still not convinced? We also learned in our research, “Lurchers can make good family dogs because they are generally gentle, affectionate, and loyal, often adapting well to family life and children.” Our lurchers are just about to turn 12 weeks old, the perfect age to start training and bonding, and they are certainly gentle, affectionate, and loyal. So live on the edge, bring home a rare dog cross that will sure to be a conversation starter.
